title: New Tariffs Target 14 Economies. Storm Delays the Macy's Parade. A FedEx Jet Overruns a Runway.
subject: New Tariffs Target 14 Economies. Storm Delays the Macy's Parade. A FedEx Jet Overruns a Runway.
preview_text: New tariff proposals, a stormy Thanksgiving, a Miami runway scare and Kim Jong Un's nuclear tour.
description: The U.S. proposed new tariffs on 14 economies. A storm pushed the Macy's parade to Saturday, and a FedEx jet overran a Miami runway.
contents_extra: Why Kim Jong Un is showing off his nuclear factories, trivia and your poll

stories.title: The United States Proposes New Tariffs on 14 Trading Partners

photo.alt: Shipping containers and cranes at a port; file photo.

paragraphs: The U.S. Trade Representative said Wednesday that 14 economies use practices tied to excess manufacturing capacity. The list includes China, the European Union, Japan, India, Korea and Vietnam. USTR said practices in those economies burden or restrict U.S. commerce.

Proposed maximum rates run from 20% to 40%, but USTR intends to cap them at levels agreed in trade deals, Reuters reports. China would face a capped 20% rate. Greer told CNBC the tariffs likely will not take effect for months, and Reuters says a public hearing is set for Jan. 25.

stories.title: A Thanksgiving Storm Pushes the Macy's Parade to Saturday

photo.alt: People with umbrellas in heavy rain; file photo.

paragraphs: Macy's postponed its 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday because of bad weather, AP reports. It is the first postponement in the parade's history. The parade will now kick off Saturday at 8:30 a.m., CBS New York reports.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani said New Yorkers could see gusts as high as 65 mph on Thursday, NBC News reports. Gov. Kathy Hochul declared a state of emergency for New York City and three nearby counties, CBS New York reports. NBC will air a rerun of the 2025 parade instead.

stories.title: A FedEx Cargo Jet Overruns a Runway at Miami International Airport

photo.alt: A jet and cargo at a gate; file photo.

paragraphs: A FedEx plane overran a runway at Miami International Airport on Wednesday night, AP reports. All but one runway closed temporarily. There were no reports of injuries, the airport said. By early Thursday, the FAA reported hourslong flight delays.

The FAA said the McDonnell Douglas MD-11 was coming from Memphis and that it is investigating, NBC News reports. FedEx said the plane had "an issue upon landing." FedEx resumed flying MD-11s in May after a UPS MD-11 crash in Kentucky last year.

stories.title: Global Stocks Rebound While Wall Street Takes Thanksgiving Off

photo.alt: A lighted stock ticker display; file photo.

paragraphs: Europe's Stoxx 600 was up 1.6% as of 4:24 a.m. ET Thursday, CNBC reports. Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 0.86%. U.S. markets are closed Thursday and will have a shortened session Friday. On Wednesday, the S&P 500 closed down 0.25% and the Nasdaq fell 0.62%.

Chip stocks led the rebound after a bruising AI-driven sell-off, CNBC reports. The head of air cargo handler SATS said AI data-centre demand shows no sign of slowing, Reuters reports. Kerry Mok said server racks and semiconductors drove air cargo growth.

deep_dive.title: Why Kim Jong Un Is Showing Off His Nuclear Factories

photo.alt: Barbed wire against a cloudy sky; file photo.

paragraphs: What happened. Kim Jong Un visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons, AP reports. State media KCNA said Thursday he inspected two nuclear materials factories, one newly opened and one being expanded. KCNA photos appeared to show centrifuges used to produce weapons-grade uranium. Some images were blurred.

Why it matters. Kim said North Korea should focus on using tactical nuclear weapons across multiple domains, Reuters reports via NBC News. Tactical weapons are generally lower-yield battlefield warheads. KCNA said he also toured a nuclear-powered equipment production base. One analyst said it may be the first look at a naval reactor program.

What each side says. Kim said North Korea's status as a nuclear weapons state is "absolutely inviolable," KCNA reported. He warned that attempts to deny that status would be seen as "an open declaration of war", Al Jazeera reports. Kim accused the U.S. of urging allies to possess nuclear-powered submarines, AP reports. Experts say he wants to show off his arsenal, AP reports.

What comes next. The tour came days after Kim ignored President Trump's offer to meet during a recent Asia visit, AP reports. Experts said Kim wants to reaffirm his rejection of talks on dismantling his program. Questions persist over prospects for renewed dialogue with the U.S., Reuters reports. North Korea did not say where the factories are.

World view: A senior Gaza education official is killed. Health officials said Israeli attacks killed at least eight Palestinians, including Khaled Abu Nada and his wife; Al Jazeera reports.
Meningitis cases climb in Gaza. Overcrowding and damaged sanitation are raising alarm about the disease among children; Al Jazeera reports.
A drone strike kills five in occupied Zaporizhia. A Russian-installed official said a Ukrainian drone hit a parking lot in Vesioloye; Al Jazeera reports.
Trump and NATO's chief warn Russia. Trump and Mark Rutte issued a joint statement Thursday urging Russia not to further expand the Ukraine war; CNBC reports.
Need to know: Iowa's lead azide blast prompts questions. Sources said the chaotic lead-up to Wednesday's detonation raised questions inside the administration about who was to blame; CBS News reports.
The Army wants to resume flights near DCA. NTSB chair Jennifer Homendy said helicopter training flights could resume as early as Dec. 1; CBS News reports.
A judge blocks a birthright citizenship order. Judge Christopher Cooper granted a preliminary injunction against Trump's latest effort to restrict it; ABC News reports.
Storms threaten holiday travel. Forecasts showed high winds and heavy rain in the Northeast, while St. Louis could see snow around the holiday; CBS News reports.
Money & markets: Inflation keeps running hot. The PCE price index rose 3.8% year over year in October, while the 10-year Treasury yield fell Wednesday; CNBC reports.
HP bucks the tech sell-off. Shares rose about 11% midday Wednesday after fourth-quarter results beat expectations; CNBC reports.
Hedge funds court everyday investors. Lower fees and smaller minimums are making hedge fund strategies more accessible, though experts warn of risks; CNBC reports.
Latin America eyes the AI boom. Data center and electrification demand is raising the value of the region's copper and energy resources; CNBC reports.
Future frontiers: Europa Clipper swings past Earth Dec. 3. The flyby will slingshot the spacecraft toward Jupiter, where it will begin orbiting in April 2030; NASA said.
Hubble maps a crowded star field. The images of the Milky Way's galactic bulge will help interpret future Roman Space Telescope observations; NASA said.
A cargo ship is due at the space station. Expedition 75 is preparing for a cargo mission arriving on Thanksgiving Day; NASA said.
SPHEREx looks through cosmic dust. A new image shows it seeing past dust at the Milky Way's center; per NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day.
The score: LeBron James posts a triple-double for Philadelphia. He had 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds as the 76ers beat Miami 111-104; ESPN reports.
Brooklyn snaps a five-game skid. Julius Randle scored 28 as the Nets beat the Bucks 104-97 in NBA Cup play; ESPN reports.
Golden State hits 20 3-pointers. De'Anthony Melton made eight of them in a 129-110 win over Sacramento; ESPN reports.
Washington scores four late goals. The Capitals beat the Flyers 7-3 after scoring four times in the final three minutes; ESPN reports.
Life & culture: Jolie and Pitt settle their winery fight. The actors said in a joint statement Wednesday that they settled the lawsuit over a French winery; ABC News reports.
Ezra Frech wins Dancing with the Stars. The two-time Paralympic gold medalist and Daniella Karagach won the season 35 trophy on Tuesday; ABC News reports.
Holiday costs squeeze families. Households face higher food, travel, heating and gift costs this season; CNBC reports.
Philadelphia cancels its Thanksgiving parade. The nation's oldest Thanksgiving parade was canceled because of dangerous weather; CBS News Philadelphia reports.

trivia.question: What time will the rescheduled Macy's parade kick off on Saturday?
trivia.explanation: B. 8:30 a.m. The parade will now kick off at 8:30 a.m. ET Saturday, NBC News reports.
